prediction_question: For a City of Melbourne pedestrian sensor, will the count in a given hour exceed a high-traffic threshold relative to that sensor's own distribution?
prediction_time: Shortly before the hour being predicted, using only prior hours, calendar position and sensor identity. The same hour's direction splits are the label source and must not be features.
target_definition: Binary: pedestriancount for the hour exceeds a per-sensor quantile threshold frozen from the training window. The threshold is not yet chosen; the per-sensor distribution must be measured first.

sources.name: City of Melbourne - Pedestrian Counting System (counts per hour)
sources.access: anonymous OpenDataSoft v2.1 API; verified live 2026-09-18, total_count 1621901

sources.name: Sensor locations dataset
sources.access: sensor_id join key and location metadata

license_evidence: LICENCE NOT CONFIRMED (re-checked 2026-09-18). GET /api/explore/v2.1/catalog/datasets/pedestrian-counting-system-monthly-counts-per-hour returns no license/licence/terms key, and its metas block carries none either.
The dataset information page HTML contains no licence text node and no creativecommons.org link; the only 'license' occurrences are OpenDataSoft feature flags, not a licence.

DataVic's CKAN harvest of the same three Pedestrian Counting System datasets (search 'pedestrian counting system monthly counts per hour', 3 matches) reports licence_id 'other-open' with license_url null. That names no terms and is not a publishable licence.
https://data.melbourne.vic.gov.au/pages/terms-of-use/ and /pages/terms/ return HTTP 404; https://www.melbourne.vic.gov.au/open-data returns HTTP 403 from this host.
The City of Melbourne commonly publishes under CC BY 4.0, but that is an assumption, not evidence. Do not make a release claim for this candidate until a licence is actually read.

Re-checked 2026-10-20 in a real browser (the earlier 403 was a user-agent block, not a dead page): melbourne.vic.gov.au/open-data loads and describes an 'open-by-default' policy with five Open Data Principles, but names no licence. Its only relevant outbound link is /copyright, which speaks about website copyright and names no data licence or Creative Commons deed. So all four channels - the open-data page, the copyright page, the OpenDataSoft dataset metadata and the DataVic harvest - are consistent: open in intent, unstated in terms.

Operator decision 2026-10-20: proceed without a readable licence - recorded in candidates/melbourne-pedestrian-counts/license.json with the five findings, the risk acceptance, attribution, and a takedown route in the dataset card. No publisher grant is claimed.
split_strategy: Temporal: earlier years train, later periods eval and holdout, with per-sensor thresholds fixed from the training window so the threshold cannot leak holdout information.

measurements.measured_on: 2026-09-18 via the portal API and information page

rejection_reason: No licence for redistribution is declared by any channel that carries this dataset (v2.1 API, dataset page, DataVic CKAN harvest), so it cannot be published - redistribution is contract 1 of dataset-discovery and it is unmet. Parked rather than dropped because the data itself is usable; only the terms are missing.
review: Unblocked by the operator on 2026-10-20 ('the license is fine'). Licence posture recorded in license.json: attribution plus takedown contact in the card, and no standard licence presented as the publisher's. Buildable now; queues behind Chicago packaging for the single worker.
next_action: Construct: hourly pulls of the OpenDataSoft v2.1 API (1,626,831 records, ~200 sensors), derive the per-sensor threshold target, freeze temporal splits, then qualify. Queue behind the Chicago package - one worker at a time.
